title: Braid-isotopic closed braids are conjugate
statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be $n$-braids and suppose
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are isotopic through closed $n$-braids
about the standard axis (an isotopy of the closed braids through braids in the
complement of the axis). Then $\beta'$ is conjugate to $\beta$ in $B_n$.
strategy: Every closed $n$-braid about the axis meets each page in exactly $n$ points, so it determines a continuous loop $c\colon S^1\to C_n(D^\circ)$ in the unordered configuration space, $\theta\mapsto$ (the $n$ intersection points with the page of angle $\theta$); for the closure of $\beta$ this loop represents $\beta$ under the published isomorphism $B_n\cong\pi_1(C_n(D^\circ))$. An isotopy of closed braids through closed braids gives a homotopy of these free loops. By the free-homotopy lemma, free homotopy classes are conjugacy classes, so the classes of $\beta$ and $\beta'$ in $B_n$ are conjugate. This is the bridge used by the survey (attributed there to Morton).

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
